# Data exploration: joint indices, census and catch reconstruction (JARA)

JABBA3 includes the data-exploration models of JARA, refitted in RTMB: a
state-space random walk with drift on log abundance (or log catch), observed
through one or several series. JARA and JABBA build the assessment story
together:

1. **catch reconstruction**: fill missing years in landings by country or fleet
   with the series-specific trends (census model) and sum them to a total catch
   with uncertainty;
2. **joint index**: combine several noisy surveys or CPUE series with different
   time spans into one relative abundance index, following the hierarchical
   analysis of multiple noisy abundance indices of Conn (2010) that is widely
   used in SEDAR assessments; JARA's relative joint index reproduces Conn's
   approach, and JABBA3 offers both forms (random walk, `state = "rw"`, and
   Conn's independent year effects, `state = "iid"`);
3. **assessment**: feed both into `jabba3()`, the joint index as the single
   index with its log-scale SE, the filled catch with a year-specific catch SE.

The model, for series $i$ in year $t$:

$$x_t = x_{t-1} + r_{b(t)} + \eta_t,\quad \eta_t \sim N(0, \sigma_p^2);\qquad
\log I_{i,t} = \log q_i + x_t + \varepsilon_{i,t},\quad
\varepsilon_{i,t} \sim N(0, se_{i,t}^2 + \sigma_{fix}^2 + \sigma_i^2)$$

- `type = "relative"`: one common state, $q_1 = 1$, the other $q_i$ estimated
  (joint index);
- `type = "census"`: one state per series with $q = 1$ (absolute catch or
  abundance by country, fleet or area), summed to a total;
- `timeblock`: the drift $r_{b(t)}$ differs before and after the block year,
  so missing values are interpolated with the block-specific trend;
- `variance.weighting`: `"model"` estimates the additional SD $\sigma_i$ by
  series, `"equal"` one common value, `"fixed"` none; `fixed.obsE` is
  $\sigma_{fix}$.

The fits use the JABBA3 diagnostics (fits, runs test, residuals, posterior
predictive checks). As everywhere in JABBA3, residual plots default to
one-step-ahead (OSA) residuals; `type = "ordinary"` gives the log residuals
used in JARA reports.

**Log-scale standard errors.** All models use observation errors on the log
scale. From a design-based SD of the untransformed index, use
$CV = sd/mean$ and $\sigma = \sqrt{\log(CV^2 + 1)}$ (close to the CV for
CV < 0.4); from a 95% interval, $\sigma = (\log(uci) - \log(lci))/(2 \times 1.96)$.

```{r jara-data}
data(jara_examples)
names(jara_examples)
```

The examples are anonymised versions of real case studies (generic series
names, multiplicative noise with a log-SD of 0.1 and random rescaling; years
and missing values unchanged): deep-water rose shrimp (*Parapenaeus
longirostris*) in GFCM GSAs 17-20 from the GFCM benchmark JARA analysis, and
southern African monkfish (*Lophius vomerinus*) survey and CPUE indices from the
2025 JARA monkfish analysis; the Dentex landings and the anglerfish CPUE are
those printed in the corresponding reports.

## A complete example: deep-water rose shrimp, GSAs 17-20

One stock, three data-exploration steps, one assessment: catches by fleet
(country and GSA) with incomplete reporting, relative survey indices by area
with log-SEs, and absolute survey biomass by area.

```{r dps-data}
dps <- jara_examples$dps
names(dps)
head(dps$catch, 3)
```

### Step 1: catch reconstruction (census with a time block)

Two fleets report only from 2012 (`fleet4`, `fleet5`). As in the benchmark
analysis, start values are assumed for 1996 (`fleet4` 10 t; `fleet5` equal to
`fleet2`) and given a larger SE (0.2) than the reported catches (0.05);
`jb3_catchfill()` takes the SE as a data frame with the same layout as the
catch. The census model interpolates each fleet between its start value and its
first report; a time block after 2016 lets the trend change when catches peaked
across the region:

```{r dps-catch, fig.height = 5}
cc <- dps$catch
cc[1, "fleet5"] <- cc[1, "fleet2"]; cc[1, "fleet4"] <- 10
sc <- cc; sc[, -1] <- 0.05; sc[1, c("fleet4", "fleet5")] <- 0.2
cf <- jb3_catchfill(cc, se = sc, timeblock = 2016)
jbplot_trend(attr(cf, "fit"))          # fleet fits and the total
```

The total catch with its year-specific log-SE: larger where the fleets with
assumed start values are interpolated:

```{r dps-catch-total, fig.height = 3.5}
jbplot_catchfill(cf)
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(cf)[c(1:3, 15:18, 24:26), c("year", "catch", "se.log", "lci", "uci")], digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

The reconstructed table (original series with the missing values replaced by
predictions, and the total):

```{r dps-catch-table}
knitr::kable(head(jb3_fill_table(cf, digits = 1), 6), row.names = FALSE)
```

### Step 2: relative joint index

The four area indices with their log-SEs, with model-estimated additional
variance by index (inverse-variance weighting):

```{r dps-joint}
ji <- jb3_trend(dps$idx, dps$idx.se, variance.weighting = "model", run = "DPS joint index")
ji
```

Diagnostics: fits and runs tests, the joint residual plot for data conflicts,
and posterior predictive checks with Bayesian p-values (near 0.5 under a
well-specified model):

```{r dps-joint-diag, fig.height = 4}
jbplot_fits(ji)
jbplot_runs(ji, type = "ordinary")
```

```{r dps-joint-resid, fig.height = 4}
jbplot_residuals(ji, type = "ordinary")
p <- jbplot_ppc(ji); attr(p, "ppc")
```

The joint index: the precision-weighted mean of the q-scaled indices by year
with its log-scale SE, and the state-space trend (red dashed):

```{r dps-joint-index, fig.height = 3.5}
jbplot_jointindex(ji)
jdx <- jb3_jointindex(ji)
knitr::kable(head(jdx, 8), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

**Random walk (JARA) or independent year effects (Conn 2010).** Conn's model
estimates the log joint index as independent year effects,
$\log U_{it} \sim N(n_t + c_i, \sigma_{p,i}^2 + \sigma_{s,it}^2)$ with
$n_t \sim N(\bar n, 1)$, the same observation model as above with
`variance.weighting = "model"`; JARA's default links the years by the random
walk. With overlapping indices they give practically the same joint index:

```{r dps-conn, fig.height = 3.5}
jc <- jb3_jointindex(jb3_trend(dps$idx, dps$idx.se, state = "iid", run = "Conn (iid)"))
ok <- is.finite(jdx$index) & is.finite(jc$index)
cmp <- data.frame(year = jdx$year[ok], rw = jdx$index[ok]/mean(jdx$index[ok]), iid = jc$index[ok]/mean(jc$index[ok]))
round(cor(log(cmp$rw), log(cmp$iid)), 3)
ggplot2::ggplot(cmp, ggplot2::aes(year)) + ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(y = rw, colour = "random walk (JARA)")) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(y = iid, colour = "iid (Conn 2010)")) + ggplot2::labs(y = "Joint index", colour = NULL) +
  theme_jabba3()
```

The independent-year-effects form needs overlapping indices to scale them
against each other; for series that do not overlap in time only the random
walk links them, through the continuity of the state.

### Step 3: census of absolute survey biomass

With absolute biomass by area (swept-area estimates), `type = "census"` models
each area separately and sums the area states to a total biomass with
uncertainty (as in Sherley et al. 2020), smoothing through missing years:

```{r dps-census, fig.height = 5}
bi <- jb3_trend(dps$bio, dps$bio.se, type = "census", run = "DPS biomass")
jbplot_trend(bi)
```

The total biomass and the relative joint index, both scaled to their means,
tell a similar story:

```{r dps-census-cmp, fig.height = 3.5}
tb <- bi$total
cmp2 <- rbind(data.frame(year = jdx$year, index = jdx$index/mean(jdx$index, na.rm = TRUE), lci = jdx$lci/mean(jdx$index, na.rm = TRUE),
                         uci = jdx$uci/mean(jdx$index, na.rm = TRUE), series = "relative joint index"),
              data.frame(year = tb$year, index = tb$est/mean(tb$est), lci = tb$lci/mean(tb$est), uci = tb$uci/mean(tb$est),
                         series = "census total biomass"))
round(cor(log(jdx$index), log(tb$est[match(jdx$year, tb$year)]), use = "complete.obs"), 2)
ggplot2::ggplot(cmp2, ggplot2::aes(year, index, colour = series, fill = series)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(ggplot2::aes(ymin = lci, ymax = uci), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) + ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::labs(y = "Index (scaled to mean)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) + theme_jabba3()
```

### Step 4: into the JABBA3 assessment

The reconstructed catch goes into `jb3_data()` with its year-specific log-SE,
which the catch error of the model uses in place of the constant `sdc`; the
joint index goes in as the single index with its `log.se` (the census total
could be used instead, or in addition, as an absolute biomass index):

```{r dps-jabba3}
d <- jb3_data(cf, jdx, stock = "DPS GSA 17-20 (anonymised)")
round(range(d$catch.se), 3)
fit <- jabba3(d, jb3_priors(d, r = c(0.8, 0.3)), jb3_model(shape = "schaefer"), run = "JARA -> JABBA3")
fit
```

```{r dps-jabba3-plot, fig.height = 9, fig.width = 10}
plot(fit)
```

The joint index is also available as an `FLIndexBiomass` with `index.var` =
log.se (`jb3_jointindex(ji, "FLIndexBiomass")`) for FLR workflows.

## Further examples

### Monkfish: joint survey indices

The South African West and South Coast surveys (`survey1`, `survey2`), from
1988, normalised by their means. With equal weighting all surveys share one
additional variance; with model weighting each survey gets its own:

```{r monk-sa, fig.height = 3.5}
mk <- jara_examples$monk
sa <- mk[mk$year >= 1988, c("year", "survey1", "survey2")]
for(v in c("survey1", "survey2")) sa[[v]] <- sa[[v]]/mean(sa[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
sa.eq  <- jb3_trend(sa, variance.weighting = "equal", run = "equal")
sa.mod <- jb3_trend(sa, variance.weighting = "model", run = "model")
rbind(equal = sa.eq$sdi, model = sa.mod$sdi)
jbplot_jointindex(sa.mod)
```

The Namibian surveys and CPUE series (`survey3`, `survey4`, `cpue1`-`cpue5`) cover
different periods, including CPUE series from old and new vessel configurations
that barely overlap; the random walk links them into one joint index:

```{r monk-nam, fig.height = 3.5}
nam <- mk[, c("year", "survey3", "survey4", "cpue1", "cpue2", "cpue3", "cpue4", "cpue5")]
nam <- nam[rowSums(is.finite(as.matrix(nam[, -1]))) > 0, ]
for(v in names(nam)[-1]) nam[[v]] <- nam[[v]]/mean(nam[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
nam.fit <- jb3_trend(nam, variance.weighting = "model", run = "Namibia")
nam.fit
jbplot_trend(nam.fit)
```

### Dentex: catch reconstruction with a time block

Dentex landings from Namibia (NAM) and Angola (ANG). Missing Angolan reports,
and the incomplete low landings from Namibia in 2009-2011 and Angola in 2012
(set to NA), are filled with the series-specific trends; the series start in
1976 and a time block after 1992 separates the decline from the later
recovery:

```{r dentex, fig.height = 3.5}
den <- jara_examples$dentex
L <- den[den$year >= 1976, ]
cf.den <- jb3_catchfill(L, se = 0.001, timeblock = 1992)
jbplot_catchfill(cf.den)
tab <- jb3_fill_table(cf.den, digits = 1)
knitr::kable(tab[tab$year %in% c(1984:1994, 2008:2013), ], row.names = FALSE)
```

### Anglerfish: two CPUE series

The last 17 years of the Portuguese and Spanish anglerfish CPUE from the JARA
joint-index report; the input SEs are very small (about 0.07), so an additional
fixed observation error of 0.1 is added:

```{r jara-ank, fig.height = 3.5}
ank <- jara_examples$ank
for(v in c("POR", "ESP")) ank[[v]] <- ank[[v]]/mean(ank[[v]][ank$year > 2009], na.rm = TRUE)
ank.fit <- jb3_trend(ank, jara_examples$ank.se, fixed.obsE = 0.1, run = "ANK")
jbplot_jointindex(ank.fit)
```
